fig1_pv_path_areas.svg: Three quasiequilibrium paths from 0.1 to 0.3 m$^3$ starting at 3 bar, with the area under each shaded. The legend values come from work_pdV, the trapezoid rule applied to the SAMPLED path, and each one is asserted against its closed form (work_isobaric, work_isothermal_ideal_gas, work_polytropic) inside this script. The ordering is the general rule: the higher the polytropic exponent, the faster the pressure decays as the gas expands, and the less work the same volume change returns.
fig2_cycle_enclosed_area.svg: Why engines are drawn as loops. Expanding along the upper path delivers 33.0 kJ and returning along the lower one costs 19.8 kJ, so the cycle nets 13.2 kJ — exactly the enclosed area, evaluated here by applying work_pdV to each leg and adding. The sign follows the direction of travel: clockwise produces work, anticlockwise consumes it, which is the only difference between an engine and a heat pump on this diagram. Since the cycle returns to its start, $\Delta U=0$ and the first law makes this net work equal to the net heat.
